label: input token i (copy phase, and first position)
explanation: Token detector for input i. Fires on every copy-phase step whose input is i (the model feeding back its own output i), strongly: about 0.7-1.0 of max, with doubled ii and earlier recall positions among the top examples. It also fires on every i at t=0, but weakly and with a fixed value (~0.19 of max). An i elsewhere in the original phase (t>0) gives only a weak, occasional activation (~0.1-0.2), and those are most of the misses (about 1% of activation mass). Never fires on the delimiter. Essentially no activation on other tokens (tiny ~0.1 blips on x/b/g). Dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.95, mass recall 0.99. Plain in_tok==i gets recall 0.98 but precision 0.56, because most original-phase i do not fire.

issues: Minor: the misses (5% of active steps, about 1.1% of mass) are mostly original-phase i at t>0. They sit mainly at t=1, where i fires 13% of the time at about 0.12 of max; at t>1 it is rarer. Together these steps have precision 0.038 and mass 0.006. The explanation already describes them as weak and occasional, and adding t=1 would cost far more precision than the recall it gains.
Minor: non-i tokens make up 2.2% of active steps but only 0.4% of mass, and their precision is 0.0004. The explanation's 'tiny blips on x/b/g' covers this.

Verified on dev: i in the copy phase has precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.946. i at t=0 has precision 1.0 at about 0.19 of max. The feature never fires on the delimiter. On test: P=1.0, R=0.947, F1=0.973, mass recall 0.989, matching the reported scores.
